name: Trompe-l'oeil
summary: Painted perspective that continues the real room, so that a flat wall or ceiling seems to open into space.
how: Set the vanishing point at the eye of a viewer who stands at one marked spot in the room.
Continue the real cornice, columns and arches in paint for 1 to 3 storeys of false height.
Paint the sky or the open part with the lightest value; keep the painted frame at the value of the real stone.

origin.note: Andrea Mantegna paints an open oculus with figures that look down into the Camera degli Sposi (1465 to 1474).

adoptions.via: Giulio Romano paints the Sala dei Giganti in Mantua so that the walls and the vault seem to fall on the viewer.
Andrea Pozzo paints a false dome and an open vault over the nave of Sant'Ignazio in Rome.

sources.title: Martin Kemp, The Science of Art (1990)
Andrea Pozzo, Perspectiva pictorum et architectorum (1693)
